To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
“Our key-value memory network system achieved better performance than the baseline knowledge-driven approach for clinical question answering using clinical notes and descriptions.

1) our clinical question answering (CQA) system performed well for the TREC 2016 CDS track and 2) our knowledge graph-based system performed better with summaries whereas our key-value network-based system performed better on notes and descriptions.

our clinical question answering systems achieved best or near-best performance for 20% and better than median performance for 40% topics across all participants for all evaluation measures and our key-value memory networks performed better with notes than the knowledge graph-based approach.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design of a hybrid system that combines the strengths of knowledge-driven and deep learning-based approaches for the task of clinical question answering.
developing a clinical question answering system using a combination of deep learning and knowledge-driven approaches for answering generic clinical queries.
the development of clinical question answering (QA) systems that can retrieve relevant biomedical articles from a corpus of scientific literature to answer a given clinical question.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
our system is competitive with the best performing systems for the majority of topics and outperforms the best performing systems on a significant portion of topics.

the best performing systems for the clinical decision support track at TREC 2016 are those which use the knowledge graph for diagnostic inferencing, and those that use key-value memory networks for biomedical document retrieval.

the key-value memory network outperformed the baseline knowledge graph-based system across all three question formats, whereas the baseline knowledge graph system with summaries outperformed the key-value memory networks with summaries.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
our clinical question answering systems are capable of answering generic clinical questions with high performance.
the key-value memory network is a powerful deep learning model for clinical question answering, and the knowledge graph can help to further boost the performance.
we are the only team that submitted runs using knowledge graph-based and memory network-based approaches.
The main takeaway from our work is that
knowledge-driven approaches can complement deep learning-based approaches to improve the clinical question answering performance.
knowledge-driven systems can be competitive with deep learning-based models when the knowledge graph is well-curated and the clinical scenarios are sufficiently well-defined.
a combination of knowledge-based and deep learning-based approaches can be effectively applied to clinical question answering.
